name: French Marigold
grown_as: A half-hardy annual raised under cover, often planted among crops. William's library lists 'Boy-O-Boy' mix: a dwarf, bushy type about 20 cm high with double, crested flowers in yellow, orange and red, some two-coloured. Drawn in orange. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A low, bushy, much-branched annual 15 to 30 cm high, the stems often purplish. The whole plant has a strong, sharp smell when touched.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite lower down, sometimes alternate near the top
leaf.type: Compound: pinnate, with about 9 to 13 leaflets along a central stalk and one at the end
leaf.outline: The whole leaf oblong, 4 to 9 cm; each leaflet narrow lance-shaped, 1 to 2.5 cm
leaf.base: Leaflets stalkless on the central stalk
leaf.margin: Fine, sharp teeth all along each leaflet
leaf.veins: A midrib in each leaflet; little else visible
leaf.surface: Smooth and hairless, dotted near the edges with tiny clear oil glands that show against the light

flower.form: A double, crested head: a ring of broad flat rays round a raised crest of short, frilled florets
flower.petals: Outer rays broad, rounded and wavy, often with a velvety red-brown blotch; the crest is a tight cushion of short frilly florets
flower.colour: Orange, yellow or gold, some red-brown with gold edges
flower.centre: The raised frilly crest, the same colour as the rays or darker
flower.behind: A smooth, slim green tube of bracts joined together, faintly ribbed, ending in five short points, dotted with oil glands
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of the stems on short stalks that swell under the head, facing up

fruit: The bract tube dries brown, with a brush of seeds poking out of the top. Each seed is thin and needle-like, 6 to 10 mm, black with a straw-coloured bristly tip.
seedling: Two narrow, oblong seed leaves on a purplish stem. The first true leaves are already cut into toothed leaflets and smell when touched.
winter: Nothing: killed by the first frost.

leaf: leaf divided into many narrow pointed leaflets along a central stalk
fine sharp teeth all along each leaflet
bloom: raised frilly crest in the middle
smooth slim tube of joined bracts behind, with small points at the top
seedling: two narrow seed leaves on a purplish stem
first leaves already divided into leaflets
young: low bushy plant with many stems
flower: many small double orange and yellow flowers just above the leaves
seedhead: tuft of black seeds with pale tips showing at the top

look_alikes: African marigold (Tagetes erecta) is taller with large ball-shaped heads. Signet marigold (Tagetes tenuifolia) has very fine leaves and tiny single flowers. Calendula has soft simple leaves, flat bracts and curled seeds.
